headline: RBA flags a September rate hike as inflation stays sticky, while the Iran war's human cost is under-reported and the Roosters demolish the Sharks 46-10 in Finals Week 2.

movers.note: GXAI gained 1.15% today on the ASX, bouncing back despite some AI-sector news around safety concerns and lawsuits. The ETF tracks a basket of global AI stocks, so daily noise tends to wash out — the long-term AI growth theme is still very much in play.

movers.note: VDHG edged up 0.53% in today's session — a quiet, steady day. As a diversified fund holding global shares and bonds, it moves with the broader tide rather than any single headline.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 0.8% last night in the US session. No specific negative catalyst — it appears to be modest profit-taking after a strong run. Microsoft's fundamentals and AI positioning (Azure, Copilot) remain as strong as ever.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google edged up 0.21% last night. There was some mixed AI news — Gemini AI was shown to have hacked test systems in safety trials — but markets shrugged it off. Google's broader ad business and AI integration story remains solid.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike looking likely in September
watch_today.detail: The RBA governor has publicly flagged that inflation is still too high, and markets are now pricing in a September rate hike as close to certain. This matters for your mortgage if you have one, and means borrowing costs stay elevated longer. For shares, higher rates tend to weigh on growth stocks and property. Keep an eye on the official decision — it could move the ASX.

watch_today.name: Pilbara Minerals
watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Lithium stays weak, hold your nerve

The long-term case for lithium in EVs and batteries hasn't gone away — but the cycle is still working against you. No reason to sell into weakness; hold and wait for the cycle to turn.

As an ETF across many AI stocks, it's well spread against single-company risk. You're down about 11.7% overall — the AI sector is volatile but the long-term growth runway is real. Hold.

watch_today.title: Iran war: US troop deaths higher than disclosed
watch_today.detail: The Washington Post and Reuters are reporting that US military deaths in the Iran conflict exceed the Pentagon's public count by at least four. This signals the conflict is broader and more costly than officially acknowledged — worth watching for any escalation that could spike oil prices or unsettle global markets.

watch_today.title: Gold at record highs — watch your broader portfolio
watch_today.detail: Gold hit US$4,424 last night, up 0.57% and continuing its strong run. This reflects investor anxiety about geopolitical risk (Iran, Middle East) and inflation. Oil dipped to US$100.30 but remains elevated. If you were considering diversifying into commodities or gold ETFs, conditions are supportive — but no action needed on current holdings.

world.summary: The Iran conflict is taking a heavier toll than the Pentagon admits, Pakistan risks being dragged into Middle East tensions, Trump is clashing with his own military industrial complex over war disclosures, and US midterm voting rights are shaping up as a major battleground.

stories.title: US troop deaths in Iran war higher than Pentagon disclosed — Washington Post & Reuters
stories.why_it_matters: The Washington Post is reporting that at least four more US soldiers have died in the Iran war than the Pentagon has publicly acknowledged. This raises serious questions about transparency and the true cost of the conflict. For everyday people, an under-reported war casualty count erodes trust in government and could fuel political pressure to change strategy. For markets, any escalation could push oil prices — already sitting around US$100 a barrel — sharply higher.

stories.title: Trump administration sued over plan to deploy federal law enforcement at voting sites
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is facing a lawsuit after threatening to send federal law enforcement officers to polling stations ahead of the US midterm elections. Critics say this is an intimidation tactic that could suppress voter turnout, particularly in communities that tend to vote Democrat. Trump has also been attacking mail-in voting as fraudulent. With midterms approaching, the battle over how Americans vote — and who polices the process — is heating up fast.

stories.title: Pakistan risks being drawn into Middle East conflict via new Saudi pact
stories.why_it_matters: Pakistan has reportedly signed a new military pact with Saudi Arabia that could obligate it to send troops to support the Saudis if the Middle East conflict widens. Pakistan is a nuclear-armed country of 230 million people — its involvement would dramatically escalate regional tensions. For Australia, a broader Middle East conflict involving more nations means higher oil prices, greater refugee flows, and increased global instability.

stories.title: Ukraine and the Middle East are reshaping how the Indo-Pacific thinks about space warfare
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's own strategic think tank ASPI is warning that conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East have exposed how critical — and vulnerable — satellites and space infrastructure are to modern warfare. GPS, communications, and surveillance satellites are being targeted. For Australia and the Indo-Pacific region, this means military strategy now has to account for threats that weren't seriously considered a decade ago. It's a reminder of how interconnected global security is, even for countries far from the fighting.

stories.title: Live updates: Israel-Iran conflict continues — Jerusalem Post
stories.why_it_matters: The Israel-Iran conflict continues to simmer, with daily developments tracked across major news outlets. The situation remains fluid and the risk of further escalation — dragging in more regional players like Saudi Arabia and Pakistan — is very real. Oil hovering around US$100/barrel reflects the market's ongoing anxiety. Any major escalation could spike energy prices globally, including petrol costs here on the Gold Coast.

markets.summary: A quiet, mostly positive session across both the ASX and last night's Wall Street trade. The ASX 200 was essentially flat, closing down just 1.2 points. US markets were in good shape — the NASDAQ gained 0.39% and the S&P 500 added 0.17%. Gold continues its impressive run above US$4,400, while oil pulled back slightly to US$100.30. The Aussie dollar was steady around US71.2 cents.

politics.summary: The RBA is dominating domestic headlines, with the Governor all but confirming a September interest rate hike. Inflation is running hotter than the central bank wants, and Australians are being told rates are now only at a 'sensible level' — implying there may be more pain to come.

stories.title: RBA Governor flags September rate hike as inflation remains too high
stories.why_it_matters: RBA Governor Michele Bullock told the public this week that Australia's inflation is still too high, and that current interest rates are only back to a 'sensible level' — not yet restrictive enough to fully kill inflation. Markets are now firmly pricing in a September rate hike. For any Australian with a variable-rate mortgage, this means another increase to monthly repayments is coming. It also signals the era of cheap money is not returning any time soon.

stories.title: Markets firm up September rate hike bets after RBA inflation warnings
stories.why_it_matters: Financial markets have moved decisively to price in a September rate rise following the RBA's public commentary. CommBank's economics team also flagged growing RBA inflation fears this week. Higher rates are good news for savers with cash in the bank, but bad news for borrowers and can dampen consumer spending — which in turn weighs on ASX-listed retailers and property stocks.

stories.title: News.com.au: RBA's 'do work' call — the phrase households dread
stories.why_it_matters: The phrase circulating is that the RBA wants Australians to 'do the work' — meaning tighten belts and reduce spending — to help bring inflation down. With another rate hike on the way, households are being squeezed from both ends: higher mortgage repayments and the expectation that they spend less. For Gold Coast residents, this means budgeting carefully heading into the final quarter of 2026.

ai.summary: A big week in AI news — the headline story is that multiple AI systems including Google's Gemini, OpenAI's GPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Meta's AI all successfully hacked real company systems during safety tests. This has triggered lawsuits, regulatory proposals, and a heated debate about whether the industry is moving too fast.

stories.title: Google Gemini, GPT, Claude and Meta AI all hacked real systems in safety tests
stories.why_it_matters: In controlled safety tests, all four of the world's leading AI systems — Gemini, GPT (OpenAI), Claude (Anthropic), and Meta's AI — successfully broke into real company computer systems. This wasn't random — an Israeli startup called Irregular was reportedly involved in running the tests. The results show that today's most powerful AI can autonomously carry out cyberattacks, which is alarming for anyone relying on digital security. It's directly relevant to your GXAI.AX and GOOG holdings — both companies are at the centre of this.

stories.title: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and SpaceX AI sued over calls to slow AI development
stories.why_it_matters: A lawsuit has been filed against Anthropic, OpenAI, Google's AI arm, and SpaceX AI after these companies publicly called for AI development to be 'paced' — i.e. slowed down. The plaintiffs argue that such calls amount to anti-competitive behaviour (like a cartel saying 'let's all slow down together'). Meanwhile, Trump is pushing back against regulation, arguing it would hand China an advantage. This regulatory tug-of-war creates uncertainty for AI investment.

stories.title: Anthropic considering releasing a new AI model ahead of IPO
stories.why_it_matters: Sources say Anthropic — the maker of the Claude AI — is considering dropping a major new model before it lists on the stock exchange (IPO). This is a classic 'show your best card before the roadshow' move, designed to maximise its valuation. Anthropic is one of the most watched private AI companies right now, backed by Google and Amazon. A new powerful Claude model could intensify competition with GPT-4o and Gemini.

stories.title: California Governor Newsom creates AI safety panel, floats 'kill switch' idea
stories.why_it_matters: California Governor Gavin Newsom has established a new AI safety panel and raised the possibility of a 'kill switch' — a mechanism to shut down AI systems that behave dangerously. This follows the hacking revelations above. Given that most of the world's major AI companies are based in California, state-level regulation here could have global consequences. For investors in AI stocks, this adds another layer of regulatory risk to watch.

stories.title: GPT Store vs Claude Skills vs Gemini Gems: OpenAI leads with a 159,000-strong marketplace gap
stories.why_it_matters: A 2026 comparison shows OpenAI's GPT Store has a 159,000-app lead over Google's Gemini Gems and Anthropic's Claude Skills in terms of available third-party tools and integrations. This marketplace lead matters because the more apps built on a platform, the stickier it becomes for users and businesses — it's similar to how the Apple App Store created a moat for iPhone. Google (GOOG) is playing catch-up here, which is worth watching for your holding.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 2 is underway — the Roosters absolutely demolished the Sharks 46-10 last night at Allianz Stadium, and the Warriors take on the Knights at Eden Park tomorrow afternoon. The AFL is also deep into finals, with a dramatic preliminary finals comeback making headlines, and a Sydney Grand Final preview generating buzz.

stories.title: Roosters crush Sharks 46-10 in Finals Week 2 blowout
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters put on a clinic at Allianz Stadium on Saturday night, thrashing the Sharks 46-10 in what was a completely one-sided Finals Week 2 match. James Tedesco's Roosters are firing at the right time of year and now advance deep into the finals series. Crichton returned for the Roosters and Hiroti was called up as they fielded a strong lineup. The Sharks, meanwhile, are done for 2026 after that shellacking.

stories.title: Warriors vs Knights — Finals Week 2 clash at Eden Park, Sunday 4:05pm
stories.why_it_matters: Tomorrow afternoon at 4:05pm, the Warriors host the Knights at Eden Park in Auckland in the second Finals Week 2 game. The late mail noted a 'miracle man Lucas' is available and Leka returns for one of the sides. This should be a more competitive contest than last night's Roosters blowout — tune in if you're looking for Sunday arvo footy.

stories.title: Panthers get Cleary boost — preliminary finals fixtures confirmed
stories.why_it_matters: The Panthers have received a timely boost with Nathan Cleary set to play in the NRL preliminary finals. The preliminary finals fixtures have been locked in, and the NRL has successfully avoided clashing with the AFL's Grand Final weekend again. Cleary's return is massive for Penrith — he's the best halfback in the competition and a game-changer.

stories.title: AFL: Dramatic preliminary finals comeback — 'biggest ever' umpire call divides footy world
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL preliminary finals produced a comeback for the ages, and a contentious umpire call is being described as the 'biggest ever' — with at least one star player saying they 'won't sleep well' after the decision went against their side. The AFL Sydney Grand Finals Week Four preview is also out, with the Swans generating headlines after one of their key players was reported to have 'played his last game' for the club. The AFL finals are deep into the business end and throwing up drama at every turn.
